summary: A wiki note excerpt from a fiction book (Book 10, part 55) following a couple, Trish and her date, driving from San Luis Obispo toward a cemetery for a tombstone unveiling that his mother is organizing. They phone his mother for directions, get lost, and buy a map, while the man frets about being late. The conversation turns playful and flirtatious as Trish teases him about bringing a date to an unveiling and his nervousness, and the excerpt ends mid-sentence.
one_line: Trish and her date drive from San Luis Obispo to a cemetery tombstone unveiling, getting lost on bad directions from his mother and bantering flirtatiously.
key_facts: The couple needs directions from San Luis Obispo to the cemetery for a tombstone unveiling.
The man's mother gives the directions over the phone, including left, then right, then left, then a slight left, then up the hill.
The woman says she has no clue where they are going and they pull off at the next exit to buy a map.
The man says they are going to be late, and the woman says they now have an excuse because his mother knows they are late.
Once on the secondary roads, the highway full of stopped cars gives way to waves, beach and palms.
The woman asks whether a cemetery is the kind of place one brings a date to.
The man says, "We're not burying anyone," and that it is "just an unveiling."
The woman jokes that she keeps picturing his mom cutting a ribbon with giant gold scissors.
The man admits he is a pedantic nature and says appealing to it to distract him is a cheap trick.
The man puts his hand up the vent of the woman's apron-trousers and over her thigh, and she responds "Achtung!"
The couple has had only eight dates, 20-some phone calls and about 100 emails before this outing.
The woman squeezes the man's hand tight enough to make his knuckles grind together to get him back on topic.
The woman asks him to finish explaining tombstone-unveiling, and she pretends not to have seen the surfers.
